title: The Origins of Corruption in Ukraine: Socio-Legal Aspects

detail.title: The Origins of Corruption in Ukraine: Socio-Legal Aspects
detail.abstract:
Abstract:

This paper examines the deep-rooted origins of corruption in Ukraine through an integrated analysis of legal and social dimensions. Despite two decades of international and national anti-corruption efforts since the establishment of International Anti-Corruption Day in 2004, corruption remains a critical challenge to Ukrainian state-building, particularly in the context of the ongoing armed conflict with the Russian Federation. The study analyzes how post-Soviet legal transformation shaped Ukraine's constitutional anti-corruption framework, revealing a persistent gap between constitutional principles of rule of law and their practical implementation. Social factors including legal nihilism, poverty, resource inequality, and systemic distrust of state institutions have normalized corrupt practices within Ukrainian society. The research demonstrates that legal reforms alone are insufficient when societal attitudes tolerate or even expect corrupt behavior from officials. The paper argues that effective anti-corruption strategy requires three interconnected approaches: developing a scientifically grounded national strategy supported by civil society; analyzing 20 years of anti-corruption efforts to establish constitutional-legal foundations; and implementing comprehensive anti-corruption education from primary school through higher education. The author, a senior investigator with practical law enforcement experience, concludes that eradicating corruption from educational institutions is essential to breaking the intergenerational transmission of corrupt practices. The study emphasizes that Ukraine's victory in the war against Russian aggression must be accompanied by parallel victory in the domestic war against corruption.​

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there is no conflict of interest—financial, institutional, or personal—that could be perceived to influence the research, analysis, or conclusions presented in this study. This article, “Whoosh in the Perspective of Public Service: Between State Mission and Policy Misformulation”, was prepared independently by the author in his capacity as a public policy researcher and consultant, without any sponsorship, funding, or affiliation from government institutions, political parties, or corporations involved in the Jakarta–Bandung High-Speed Railway (Whoosh) project. The research was conducted purely for academic and policy analysis purposes, with the objective of strengthening public understanding of Indonesia’s public service and procurement policy frameworks under Law No. 25/2009 on Public Service and related regulations.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This research did not involve any human participants, experiments, or confidential institutional data, and therefore did not require prior ethical approval from any ethics committee. The analysis was based entirely on publicly available sources, including official laws, government regulations, financial reports, and credible public media, which were all cited according to academic and legal standards. The author confirms that the study complies with the principles of research integrity, including transparency, accountability, and academic independence, consistent with the Singapore Statement on Research Integrity (2010) and the SSRN Research Integrity Policy.
declarations.funderStatement: The author declares that this study received no financial support or funding from any institution, public or private, including government agencies, state-owned enterprises, or international organizations. All stages of research—including conceptualization, data collection, legal review, and manuscript preparation—were conducted using the author’s own resources as part of his independent research activities on public policy and procurement systems in Indonesia. The absence of external funding ensures that the analysis, conclusions, and recommendations in this paper reflect the author’s independent and objective judgment.
declarations.clinicalTrialRegistration: This study does not involve any clinical trial or human experimentation, and therefore no clinical trial registration number applies. The paper is based on policy and regulatory analysis concerning public service and government procurement systems in Indonesia, conducted through document-based research and secondary data from public sources. Accordingly, no registration under any clinical trial registry (e.g., ClinicalTrials.gov, EU-CTR, or WHO ICTRP) is required or relevant for this type of policy research.

detail.abstract: The Jakarta–Bandung High-Speed Railway Project (KCJB), known as Whoosh (an acronym for Waktu Hemat, Operasi Optimal, Sistem Hebat), stands as the largest public transportation project in modern Indonesian history. Although President Joko Widodo stated that Whoosh represents a form of public service—measured not by financial profit but by social benefit—the policy formulation and implementation reveal otherwise. The project was executed through a business-to-business (B2B) partnership between Indonesian state-owned enterprises (SOEs) and Chinese corporations, based on Presidential Regulation No. 107 of 2015 (Perpres/107/2015). This structure deviates from the principles of public service under Law No. 25 of 2009 on Public Service (UU/25/2009) and the transparency and competition principles of Presidential Regulation No. 54 of 2010 on Government Procurement (Perpres/54/2010). This paper integrates two analytical frameworks: (1) Thomas R. Dye’s policy cycle to identify the misformulation of the Whoosh project; and (2) William N. Dunn’s evaluation framework to formulate corrective policy options. Findings show that Whoosh should have been categorized as a public service assignment under Article 5 paragraph (4) letter a of UU/25/2009, not a commercial infrastructure project.

title: AI and Operational Losses: Evidence from U.S. Bank Holding Companies
affiliations: Federal Reserve Banks - Quantitative Supervision & Research and

detail.title: AI and Operational Losses: Evidence from U.S. Bank Holding Companies
detail.abstract: This study demonstrates that banking organizations with higher AI investments are exposed to more operational risk. Using comprehensive supervisory data on operational losses from large U.S. bank holding companies (BHCs) combined with detailed company-level data on AI-skilled human capital, we show that BHCs with more AI investments suffer higher operational losses per dollar of total assets. The impact of AI investments on operational losses significantly varies by loss type and is driven by external fraud, client-related issues, and system failures. These losses stem not only from small, frequent incidents but also from severe, tail-risk events. The risk-enhancing effect of AI is more pronounced for BHCs with weaker risk management practices. Our findings have important implications for banking performance, risk, and supervision.

title: Aleatory and Epistemic Uncertainty Across Probability, Finance, and Domain Theory

detail.title: Aleatory and Epistemic Uncertainty Across Probability, Finance, and Domain Theory
detail.abstract: Uncertainty in quantitative reasoning divides naturally into two kinds: aleatory (irreducible variability of the world) and epistemic (incompleteness of knowledge). We show how this dichotomy manifests across disciplines: in frequentist and Bayesian statistics, in control and filtering, in financial mathematics, and finally in domain theory via the probabilistic powerdomain. In each setting, aleatory uncertainty appears as measure-theoretic randomness, while epistemic uncertainty appears as order-theoretic approximation or informational incompleteness. We conclude that the two notions form orthogonal but composable structures: the probabilistic powerdomain provides the semantic space where they coexist. We then give a formal construction: the valuations powerdomain V(D) is the free convex (barycentric) algebra over a continuous dcpo D, with unit η : D → V(D) (Dirac embedding) and multiplication µ : VV(D) → V(D) (integration). Aleatory uncertainty appears as convex mixture (via the monad's algebra), while epistemic uncertainty appears as directed joins in D. We express Bayesian conditioning and the Kalman filter as Kleisli maps for the valuations monad, making the decomposition operational and compositional.

title: Britain's Debt Restructuring, 1717-22

detail.title: Britain's Debt Restructuring, 1717-22

publicationDetails.detailsText: FRB of Chicago Working Paper No. 2025-21
publicationDetails.journalName: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Britain’s debt was nil in 1688 and 60% of GDP in 1717. From 1717 to 1722 the debt was restructured, including through the South Sea operation of 1720. I discuss the reasons for the restructuring and the tensions it revealed between taxpayers and creditors. The South Sea bubble turned the operation into an ex-post Ponzi scheme and redistributed among creditors, from late to early entrants, and from creditors to taxpayers. Parliament intervened to redistribute among creditors (but far less than was feasible) and, very reluctantly, from taxpayers to creditors. Commitment to honor the debt was still weak thirty-five years after the Glorious Revolution.

detail.title: International Arbitrators as a Profession
detail.abstract: This article argues that international arbitrators now satisfy the sociological criteria of an established profession. This conclusion is not based on the classical, state-licensed definition of a profession but on more modern defections that identify professions as including transnational, networked community that consolidates authority through specialized expertise, reputational gatekeeping, and peer-policed ethics. Building on contemporary theories of transnational professionalization, this article argues that a shared arbitrator identity, formalized training pathways (e.g., CIArb, institutional academies, specialized LLMs), and soft-law self-governance (IBA Guidelines, institutional challenge decisions) collectively replicate the core functions of professional self-regulation. The article engages João Ilhão Moreira's contrary view, reframing decentralization, hybrid roles, and the absence of licensing as key features of emergent global professions. It then traces how arbitrators' jurisdiction and public recognition have expanded, and assesses pressure points-ISDS reform, CAS/EU judicial oversight, and corruption cases such as P&ID v. Nigeria-where professional responsibility must be exercised to sustain legitimacy. The conclusion calls for arbitrators to lean into their professional status by embracing transparent procedures, ethical commitments, and a more coordinated public voice to shape the future of global dispute resolution.

title: Section 1031’s Beneficial Effect on the Real Estate Life Cycle

detail.title: Section 1031’s Beneficial Effect on the Real Estate Life Cycle

publicationDetails.detailsText: Brooklyn Law School, Legal Studies Paper No. 805
publicationDetails.journalName: Brooklyn Law School Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This article describes the important role of section 1031 of the Internal Revenue Code in the life cycle of real estate. Real estate is developed, ages, needs renovation, and ages again. Each stage of the life cycle of real estate requires specialized skills. Section 1031 helps real estate be owned by persons with the appropriate skills at each stage of the property’s like cycle. This article shows that section 1031 thus helps stimulate the economy and make real estate available for its highest and best use.

title: Liquidity and Speculation in Laboratory Markets with Production and Trade
affiliations: James Madison University and University of Virginia - Department of Economics

detail.title: Liquidity and Speculation in Laboratory Markets with Production and Trade
detail.abstract: This paper uses a laboratory experiment to study how investment costs and excess liquidity affect capital investment.  Subjects produce and trade capital goods in a multiperiod market with capital depreciation.  Treatments vary the marginal cost of investment, aggregate cash level, and relative cash endowments of individual subjects. Increasing aggregate cash increases price bubbles and increases excess production of capital goods, relative to a social optimum.  Subjects with higher individual cash endowments are less likely to make privately optimal production decisions.  In contrast to q-theory’s predictions, cash holdings significantly affect unconstrained subjects’ production decisions.

title: Women at the Top, Quotas, and Competence Expectations: Evidence from an Information Experiment

detail.title: Women at the Top, Quotas, and Competence Expectations: Evidence from an Information Experiment

declarations.funderStatement: Financial support and assistance from GrEELab (Groningen Experimental Economics Laboratory at the University of Groningen) is gratefully acknowledged.

detail.abstract: The term "quota woman" carries a negative connotation, suggesting that women appointed under quota policies lack competence. However, research shows that quotas attract high-ability women and promote them without reducing efficiency (Balafoutas and Sutter, 2012; Niederle et al., 2013). Public opinion may diverge from these findings for several reasons. First, people may lack knowledge about the precise quota setting. Second, people may not anticipate behavioral responses such as high-ability women entering quota-competitions. Third, people may find it difficult to internalize scientific evidence. This study contributes to the literature by ruling out the first mechanism by design and providing clean experimental evidence on the second and the third. Our experiment had two treatments. Treatment NoInfo explained only the setting of a gender quota experiment, while treatment Info added information about quotas attracting high-ability women to competitions who might otherwise avoid them. In both treatments, we elicited subjects' expectations of the competence of women who won under a) no quotas and b) quotas. In treatment NoInfo women were expected to be less competent if they won under a quota. However, in treatment Info participants evaluated "quota women" more positively. These results show that people do not intuitively recognize quotas' ability to attract high-ability women, but they can grasp this channel and adjust their expectations when made aware.

reference: Forthcoming in CHALLENGES OF EUROPEAN REFUGEE AND ASYLUM LAW AND POLICY (Iris Goldner Lang and Janine Silga eds., Oxford University Press, 2026)
title: Silver Linings of the EU Migration Pact: Progressive Elements and Binding Solidarity
affiliations: University of California, Berkeley Law School and University of California, Berkeley - School of Law

detail.title: Silver Linings of the EU Migration Pact: Progressive Elements and Binding Solidarity

publicationDetails.detailsText: Forthcoming in CHALLENGES OF EUROPEAN REFUGEE AND ASYLUM LAW AND POLICY (Iris Goldner Lang and Janine Silga eds., Oxford University Press, 2026)

detail.abstract:
After eight years of political deadlock, the European Parliament’s approval of the EU Migration Pact in April 2024 marked a watershed moment in European asylum policy.  The ten legislative texts adopted to reform EU migration and asylum policy emerged from what many observers described as an impossible political landscape—one characterized by rising far-right influence, mounting public skepticism toward migration, and seemingly irreconcilable differences between member states on fundamental questions of solidarity and responsibility-sharing.

Although the Pact has many conservative elements, given the political climate in Europe and around the world, it is also important to flag its progressive elements. This chapter outlines the specific, incremental changes that benefit asylum seekers and examines how intra-EU solidarity operates between Central and Peripheral states. While the main (and intended) beneficiaries of intra-EU solidarity are member states, we argue that it also benefits asylum seekers, as no asylum seeker thrives in overcrowded closed detention centers at the European periphery and many prefer to move to more central European countries. This chapter demonstrates that even within highly restrictive political environments, meaningful progressive innovations can emerge through technical policy development, institutional creativity, and strategic compromise, providing both immediate benefits to asylum seekers and foundations for future advancement.

Understanding the Migration Pact’s progressive dimensions serves several critical purposes. First, it provides a more balanced assessment of the Pact’s actual impact on refugee protection in Europe, moving beyond the polarized narratives that have dominated public discourse. Second, it identifies concrete achievements that advocates can use as benchmarks for national implementation and could further strengthen through litigation before the Court of Justice of the European Union. Third, it offers valuable insights into how progressive policy innovations can emerge even within politically constrained environments characterized by rising nationalism and anti-immigrant sentiment.

title: Fleet Allocation for Shared Mobility Systems with Endogenous Demand and Network Effects
affiliations: School of Management, Northwestern Polytechnical University, School of Management, Northwestern Polytechnical University, Rotman School of Management,  and Northwestern Polytechnic University (NPU)

detail.title: Fleet Allocation for Shared Mobility Systems with Endogenous Demand and Network Effects
detail.abstract: Fleet allocation is critical for the profitability and service quality of shared mobility systems, yet most planning models overlook how user demand is shaped by station inventory availability on a network. This paper aims to prescribe fleet allocation decisions by incorporating the availability-aware user behaviors. We propose a data-driven pipeline that integrates the inventory responsive user choice model and network resource allocation for shared mobility systems. Specifically, we model user station choice through the multinomial logit framework and embed it within a queueing network to decide the optimal fleet distribution. We overcome the complicated nonlinear relationships by reformulating the problem as a tractable mixed-integer exponential cone program, for which we derive a provably good second-order cone approximation that significantly improves computational efficiency for practical-size networks. Empirical analysis using Citi Bike data in New York City demonstrates the efficacy of our approach, particularly in high-demand settings with a larger fleet size. Instead of allocating fleet according to observed demand, the proposed framework identifies high-potential stations in clusters by balancing inventory breadth and depth. The resulting allocation plan could better help the shared mobility system grow and sustain in the long run.

title: Learning When to Quit in Sales Conversations
affiliations: , Harvard Business School and Columbia University - Columbia Business School, Marketing

detail.title: Learning When to Quit in Sales Conversations

publicationDetails.detailsText: Cornell SC Johnson College of Business Research Paper
publicationDetails.journalName: Cornell SC Johnson College of Business Research Paper Series

publicationDetails.detailsText: Harvard Business School Marketing Unit Working Paper
publicationDetails.journalName: Harvard Business School: Marketing Unit Working Paper Series
Columbia Business School Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Salespeople frequently face the dynamic screening decision of whether to persist in a conversation or abandon it to pursue the next lead. Yet, little is known about how these decisions are made, whether they are efficient, or how to improve them. We study these decisions in the context of high-volume outbound sales where leads are ample, but time is scarce and failure is common. We formalize the dynamic screening decision as an optimal stopping problem and develop a generative language model-based sequential decision agent-a stopping agent-that learns whether and when to quit conversations by imitating a retrospectively-inferred optimal stopping policy. Our approach handles high-dimensional textual states, scales to large language models, and works with both open-source and proprietary language models. When applied to calls from a large European telecommunications firm, our stopping agent reduces the time spent on failed calls by 54% while preserving nearly all sales; reallocating the time saved increases expected sales by up to 37%. Upon examining the linguistic cues that drive salespeople's quitting decisions, we find that they tend to overweight a few salient expressions of consumer disinterest and mispredict call failure risk, suggesting cognitive bounds on their ability to make real-time conversational decisions. Our findings highlight the potential of artificial intelligence algorithms to correct cognitively-bounded human decisions and improve salesforce efficiency.

title: A Data Science Approach to Measure Gridlock in the United Nations Security Council from 1946 to 2024
affiliations: University of Geneva, University of Geneva, University of Geneva, University of Geneva and University of Geneva

detail.title: A Data Science Approach to Measure Gridlock in the United Nations Security Council from 1946 to 2024

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Professor Nicolas Levrat is the fourth Special Rapporteur on minority issues. He was appointed by the Human Rights Council on 13 October 2023 and took up his functions as Special Rapporteur on 1 November 2023.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by a research stipend from the Holcim Stiftung zur Förderung der wissenschaftlichen Fortbildung.

detail.abstract: Progress has been made in understanding the drivers of gridlock in international relations, though we lack a quantitative account of its dynamics within a single international organization. This study introduces a data-driven approach to examine how several quantitative indicators derived from the corpus of United Nations Security Council resolutions can provide insights into the presence and evolution of gridlock. We show that metrics such as text length, adoption and veto rates, voting behavior, text sentiment, and citation patterns effectively trace functional changes in Council behavior. Our analysis confirms the well-documented shift away from gridlock following the Cold War. However, we also identify a set of consistent signals, across textual, voting, and network dimensions, that point to a gradual erosion of cooperative capacity since the mid-2010s. This suggests that the Security Council may be entering a new phase of institutional stagnation, retaining sufficient resilience to avoid a return to full gridlock.

title: Technocratic versus Populist Political Orientations in Contemporary Germany: An Empirical Analysis of Ideological Clustering and Party Alignment

detail.title: Technocratic versus Populist Political Orientations in Contemporary Germany: An Empirical Analysis of Ideological Clustering and Party Alignment
detail.abstract: This paper explores how technocratic and populist orientations shape ideological positioning and party support in Germany. Drawing on recent comparative research (Bertsou, Caramani, and Koedam, 2025), I ask whether German technocratic attitudes lean toward the economic left and cultural liberalism, while populist views cluster around economically left/centrist but culturally conservative positions. Using data from the European Social Survey (ESS) and World Values Survey (WVS), I analyze how governance preferences relate to ideological self-placement and party choice. The results confirm earlier crossnational findings: k-means clustering reveals four distinct groups, with technocratically-oriented citizens (31% of sample) combining redistributive economic views with pro-immigration, cosmopolitan positions, translating into support for the Greens (β ≈-0.17, p < 0.01, CDU/CSU baseline) and SPD. Populist-oriented respondents (22% of sample) favor cultural nationalism while endorsing welfare policies, strongly predicting support for the AfD (β ≈ [INSERT NEW VALUE], p < 0.01). These patterns suggest that governance orientations represent a meaningful new dimension of competition in European democracies (Caramani, 2017; Bickerton and Invernizzi Accetti, 2021).All replication materials, including Stata and R code, are openly archived on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.17172971).

affiliations: Texas A&M University School of Law

Texas A&M University School of Law Legal Studies Research Paper
publicationDetails.journalName: Texas A&M University School of Law Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Increasingly, jurisdictions around the world are exploring and implementing proactive, management-based regulation (PMBR) as an alternative to traditional regulatory approaches that discipline attorneys after misconduct occurs. This essay examines the proof and potential of PMBR to empower lawyers and enhance public protection, while transforming the relationship between regulators and practicing lawyers. The essay is based on the Distinguished Lecture the author delivered at the Joseph G. Miller and William C. Becker Center for Professional Responsibility at the University of Akron School of Law.
